text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: SEV2 - elevated SRV/Consul lookup failures in eu-central-2c. Symptoms: internal agent 5xx/timeouts, some host-level egress errors. Pager link: https://pager.example/inc/INC-2026-0315-17

sara: Acknowledged. I’m oncall. seeing consul agent errors from nodes in euc2c: `504` to /v1/health/service/* and lots of tcp retransmit. Graphs show consul query latency spike at 02:13 UTC.

mike: Confirmed. coredns in that AZ complaining upstream: `read udp 10.0.3.5:33456->10.12.64.23:8600: i/o timeout`. That IP is a consul server in euc2c.

anjali: Any recent routing changes in euc2? I pushed a peering ACL change earlier but thought it was scoped to infra subnet only.

dave: I rolled a small BGP policy change on the edge routers at 02:05 UTC for a customer test. Reverting now.

platform-sre: Noted correlation. We see spike exactly after the BGP policy roll. Suspect route suppression to the control-plane subnet, causing cross-AZ lookups to fail when stickiness moved to euc2c.

maria: Quick impact check: internal telemetry shows ~12% error rate on internal SRV lookups for Dedicated-serving control plane during window. External customer-facing API error rate up to ~6% for ~7 minutes.

sara: Paging what we need to mitigate: restore routing to control-plane CIDR for euc2c, validate connectivity to consul servers on ports 830 / 8300 / 8500, restart affected coredns pods as fallback caching expired.

dave: Revert staged BGP change now. `sudo /usr/local/bin/bgp-rollback --change-id 20260315-01`

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollback-bgp-policy (initiated by dave)

mike: While rollback runs, I’m enabling temporary iptables accept on consul ports on nodes in euc2c to allow direct host->server reachability:
```
iptables -I INPUT 1 -p tcp -s 10.0.0.0/16 --dport 8500 -j ACCEPT
iptables -I INPUT 1 -p tcp -s 10.0.0.0/16 --dport 830 -j ACCEPT
```

anjali: Also going to cordon & restart coredns in euc2c to drop stale cache and re-resolve service SRV records. `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns --selector=topo=euc2c`

platform-sre: Rollback complete per edge controller (02:18 UTC). BGP adjacencies restored.

incident-bot: NOTE: auto-monitoring rule triggered: consul.srv_fail_rate > 5% for 2m. Alert auto-muted while oncall acknowledges.

mike: After rollback, `curl -v http://10.12.64.23:8500/v1/catalog/service/myservice` now returns 200. Consul agent metrics show reduced errors.

sara: coredns pods restarted, SRV lookup success rate recovered. Observability shows client-side retries now succeeding.

maria: Customer impact tally: 18 Dedicated tenants had degraded control-plane operations (internal agent retries) between 02:12 - 02:20 UTC. No data loss. One support ticket opened by a tenant; responding with incident summary.

dave: Root cause hypothesis: inadvertent BGP policy change suppressed route advertisement to control-plane subnet for one euc2 edge, causing intra-AZ control-plane traffic to fall back to a path through euc2c that was briefly blackholed for consul ports.

anjali: Mitigation checklist: 1) BGP rollback applied (done). 2) Restarted coredns & consul agents in euc2c to clear caches (done). 3) Temporary iptables rule (removed after test). 4) Add guardrail to deployment pipeline to block BGP policy changes without preflight.

platform-sre: Also adding a synthetic SRV probe per-AZ to catch this pattern faster. New monitor: `consul.srv_probe.az.{az} latency+status` with 30s cadence.

sara: Handoff: I’ll stay until 03:00 UTC to watch metrics and tidy follow-ups, then pass to anjali for postmortem and action items.

maria: Notifying support & CS now with templated status update: short impact summary, timeline, actions taken, ETA for full RCA.

incident-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-0315-17; severity SEV2. Playbooks: service-discovery-egress-failure.

sara: Quick notes for RCA: collect edge router configs, BGP change diff, consul server logs from 02:00-02:25 UTC (`/var/log/consul.log`), coredns logs for same window, and the pipeline change that allowed that BGP policy change.

anjali: Will own RCA. I’ll create a postmortem doc and link it in the incident ticket. Action items so far: pipeline guardrail, synthetic SRV probes per-AZ, better canary for BGP policy, and make consul port check part of our preflight.

dave: sorry about the churn. Will push a blameless timeline and the exact CLI used.

sara: thanks all. leaving summary in incident ticket and will update customers after RCA. :white_check_mark:

maria: Follow-up: support already sent an interim note. Will add final language after RCA.

platform-sre: Post-incident: schedule runbook update and add a short oncall training for BGP change process next week.

incident-bot: Incident marked: resolved -> monitoring.
